optionReasons.saa-ini-078:option:0: Aurora Serverless is relational bench on demand — not ElastiCache cache engine.
optionReasons.saa-ini-078:option:1: Memcached is cached SIMPLES multithread: without advanced structures, without persistence and without automatic failure.
optionReasons.saa-ini-078:option:2: The DAX is specific cache of DynamoDB — is not an ElastiCache engine.

finalJustifications: Because Redis offers sorted sets for rankings, lists and hashes, optional persistence and replication with automatic failover — features that simple cache does not have.
Because Redis is the only ElastiCache option compatible with SQL, allowing rankings via ORDER BY directly in the cache layer.
Because Redis persists the data in S3 for durability, recovering the advanced structures from there after any node failure.
Because Redis is the paid version of Memcached: the same behavior, with the automatic failover as a premium feature hired.

optionReasons.saa-ini-103:option:1: The multi-AZ failover switch to a SYNCRON standby — which contains the same corruption, because it replicated the bad writing.
optionReasons.saa-ini-103:option:2: The read reply also replicated corruption — promoting it does not recover the previous state.
optionReasons.saa-ini-103:option:3: The snapshot of the original creation would lose TODAS transactions since then — RPO bad.

finalJustifications: Because PITR combines automatic snapshots with transaction logs, re-creating the bank in a NOVA instance in the exact state of any second within the retention.
Because PITR undoes only the corrupted transaction, keeping the current bank in operation while the transaction log is rewritten.
Because PITR restores the latest entire backup over the current bank, returning the status to the last daily window.
Because PITR depends on the Multi-AZ standby: it is the synchronous replica that keeps the state of every minute inside the hold.

optionReasons.saa-ini-107:option:0: The DynamoDB Streams captures change events for consumption — does not restore the table to a past moment.
optionReasons.saa-ini-107:option:2: Global Tables replicate between regions for global access — would also replicate accidental exclusion.
optionReasons.saa-ini-107:option:3: The Auto Scaling adjusts read/write capacity — nothing to do with data recovery.

finalJustifications: Because PITR of the DynamoDB, once enabled, it allows restore the table for any second within up 35 days — direct protection against accidental writing/exclusion.
Because PITR keeps a complete copy of the table in each AZ of the region, and the restoration alternates to the oldest copy intact.
Because PITR block exclusions and overwrites of items without the approval of an administrator, preventing the damage to the origin.
Because PITR version each item individually as the S3 Versioning, allowing you to recover any previous version of the item.

optionReasons.saa-ini-113:option:0: A larger node has more memory, but it's still a unique point of failure.
optionReasons.saa-ini-113:option:1: Memcached has NO replication or failover — multiples we only partition cache.
optionReasons.saa-ini-113:option:2: Snapshots recover data after manually — do not automatically promote replica in case of failure.

finalJustifications: Because a replication group with Multi-AZ monitors the primary and automatically promotes a replica in another AZ, updating the endpoint without manual reconfiguration.
Because Multi-AZ divides the writings between all the nodes of the group, so the loss of the primary does not interrupt any recording.
Because the replication group restarts the primary node before any promotion, solving most flaws without failover.
Because Multi-AZ copies the cache to the S3 every minute, and the new primary is hydrated from the last snapshot saved.

optionReasons.saa-ini-121:option:0: The Aurora DO NOT wear a EBS unique location — your storage is a distributed layer of your own.
optionReasons.saa-ini-121:option:2: The Aurora makes continuous backup for the S3, but the primary durability comes from replication 6x in 3 AZs, not from S3.
optionReasons.saa-ini-121:option:3: Read Replicas Scale LEITURA and computer failure — the data durability exists in the storage layer even without any replica.

finalJustifications: Because the storage layer of Aurora replicates each data in 6 copies by 3 AZs automatically — built-in durability, independent of computer replicas.
Because Aurora record each transaction simultaneously in 6 different regions, ensuring overall durability before the commit.
Because Aurora apply RAID-6 to volumes within a single AZ, tolerating the loss of two discs without losing any data.
Because Aurora activates the traditional Multi-AZ of RDS by default, and it is the synchronous standby that guarantees the durability of the data.

optionReasons.saa-ini-124:option:0: The ALB balance of traffic HTTP/HTTPS for targets — does not manage pool of bank connections nor understands the bank protocol.
optionReasons.saa-ini-124:option:1: ElastiCache reduces repeated cache queries — does not maintain or redirect connections during failover.
optionReasons.saa-ini-124:option:2: The DMS MIGRA inter-engine/local banks — does not get in the way of application connections.

finalJustifications: Because RDS Proxy maintains a pool of connections between the application and the bank: in the failover, it preserves the connections and redirects to the new main, shortening the recovery.
Because RDS Proxy duplicates each writing to the standby instance in parallel, keeping the two copies ready for immediate failure.
Because RDS Proxy turns the bank into serverless automatically, scaling the connections along with computational capacity.
Because RDS Proxy eliminates authentication in the bank: credentials are validated once in the proxy and never sent back to the instances.

optionReasons.saa-ini-126:option:1: Multi-AZ protects inside UMA Region — does not respond to DR between regions.
optionReasons.saa-ini-126:option:2: Read replica cross-region of RDS classic has bigger lag and slower promotion — the Aurora has a custom made resource for this case.
optionReasons.saa-ini-126:option:3: Daily backup copy means RPO up to 24 HORAS — very far from 'a few seconds'.

finalJustifications: Because Aurora Global Database replica between regions typically latency < 1 second (RPO low) and allows to promote the secondary region quickly.
Because the Global Database uses synchronous replication between regions, guaranteeing RPO exactly zero in any disaster.
Because the Global Database accepts simultaneous writings in all regions by default, dispensing any manual promotion.
Because the Global Database copies daily snapshots between the Regions automatically, keeping the secondary ready to restore.

optionReasons.saa-ini-129:option:0: Restart does not change the role of the replica — it continues only reading and replicating from the main.
optionReasons.saa-ini-129:option:1: Aiming the endpoint is not enough: the replica is still REJEITA written to be promoted.
optionReasons.saa-ini-129:option:3: Multi-AZ is resilience DENTRO of the region and can be configured later — is not the step that enables written.

finalJustifications: Because the promotion turns the response into an instance INDEPENDENTE reading and writing, closing the replication with the old main — the essential step of failure.
Because the promoter reconnects the replica to the main old as standby synchronous, reversing the roles when the region returns.
Because the promoter just updates the DNS from the endpoint to the replica, which continues in read-only mode until the final synchronization.
Because the promotion restores the last snapshot shared in the secondary region, creating the new main from the backup.
